newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two Daimler Spanish plants halt production.
newsitem.headline: Two Daimler Spanish plants halt production.

text.p: German carmaker Daimler Benz's Spanish unit Mercedes Espana said on Thursday it had been forced to cease production at its two Spanish factories as a result of a truck drivers strike.
An eight-day-old strike by Spanish truckers has gripped northern Spain and prevented supplies from reaching many factories.
"Both our Vitoria and Barcelona plants are closed and will continue to be closed until we can get supplies through," said Enrique Aguirre, spokesman for Mercedes Benz Espana.
At the Vitoria plant, 2,500 of the 3,000 workers have stayed at home since Wednesday.
At the Barcelona plant, 500 of the 700 workers have not gone to work since Tuesday afternoon.
"With strikers blocking the border and abusing drivers that pass the picket line it is proving too dangerous to get supplies through," Aguirre said.
On Thursday, a convoy of trucks escorted by police attempted to deliver supplies. But Aguirre said strikers threw 20 pound rocks at the lorries, damaging the vehicles and supplies.
Mercedes Espana has applied to the government under a clause that requires it to pay 70 percent of workers' wages if a company cannot operate due to circumstances beyond its control.
